description: A post-apocalyptic survival world forty years after the collapse: no working governments, scavenger clans, water as currency, mutated wildlife, scraps of old technology. I start as a lone scavenger with a damaged water filter.

core.name: The Drought Expanse
core.tagline: Water is life. Water is power. Water is everything.
core.premise: Forty years after the Collapse, the world is a network of cracked earth, rusted steel, and choked rivers — where every drop of water is traded like gold, and survival depends on knowledge, grit, and the quiet desperation of the living.
core.tone: Gritty, grounded, immersive, with a quiet melancholy and a t
core.intro: You wake beneath a rusted overpass, the wind carrying the smell of rot and old oil. Your hands are raw from scrubbing the filter — a cracked, plastic casing with a leaky hose — and your chest aches with the weight of the day. The sky is dull gray, like a wound left open. A few miles away, the water tank at the old medical clinic leaks. Nearby, a woman in a torn raincoat is arguing with a child over a broken jug. You know what they're arguing about — the water in it. You don’t
physics: Gravity, friction, and thermodynamics function as in our world.
Water flows downhill, but scarcity makes movement dangerous — rivers are dry, lakes have evaporated or are buried under dust.
Scavenging is physically demanding: movement is slow, and every step costs energy.
Old technology fails due to corrosion, lack of power, or moisture damage — no functional batteries or generators exist.
Water cannot be created or extracted from air — only collected, stored, or traded.
impossible: Traveling through air without a water source.
Using technology that was designed to run on electricity or solar power — no re-
common_knowledge: Water is the only universally accepted currency. If you don’t have water, you are invisible.
The old world’s technology was overhyped — it didn’t last. A radio that once broadcast news now just hums, dead.

magic.summary: No magic. Only adaptation. The world has no supernatural elements. What you see is what you get — mutations are biological, not mystical.

special_rules.name: Drip Siphon Downhill Rule
special_rules.summary: A siphon can only function if it's pointed downhill. If the scavenger tries to use a siphon on a flat surface or uphill, it fails immediately and the

on_success.text: The siphon begins to draw water, a thin stream begins to flow.

on_failure.text: The siphon clicks and fails. The scavenger feels a sudden strain in their arms.

special_rules.name: Filter Maintenance
special_rules.summary: A water filter can only be used after being cleaned with dry thorn bark. Without it, it leaks and fails. Cleaning takes time and effort.

on_success.text: The filter produces a clean drop of water. The scavenger now has one bottle of usable water.

on_failure.text: The filter leaks and rusts. The scavenger loses all water from the filter.

special_rules.name: Dust Pump Handle Trade

on_success.text: The pump extracts a small stream. One full bottle is produced.

on_failure.text: The pump collapses and the scavenger’s hand is scraped. One drop of water is lost.
